correctness.rationale: Enumerating repeated-label and all-distinct outcomes yields z_i(1+z_i−S). At a fixed point the received coordinates satisfy one quadratic. For its two roots a>b, ab=p/[k(1−p)] and a+b=S+kab give the asserted converse as well: p/k=(1−p)ab<b, so the recovered x belongs to the simplex. The ratio equation gives a finite fixed-point set at each p. The weighted Cauchy–Schwarz bound makes the tangent Jacobian positive definite; its high/low splitting and group-contrast eigenvalues give instability for r≥2 and attraction exactly on the upper one-high branch, aside from the unit-eigenvalue cases. The one-high scalar increment at the uniform threshold is positive for small positive perturbations and at the fold is −Cu(u−u*)², repelling points immediately below u*. The monotone increments on these one-sided intervals and absence of intervening fixed points justify the nonlinear endpoint conclusions. Differentiating p(t) gives its sole maximum at k−1 for r=1. The map is the gradient of the stated convex potential on the simplex; the supporting-plane inequality gives a bounded Lyapunov function with increments at least half the step squared. Steps therefore vanish, every accumulation point is fixed, and an orbit with vanishing steps and a finite fixed-point accumulation set converges. Exact substitution of t=3 and t=4/3 gives the rational witness and stated spectra; the r=2 branch stays below p_lin in this example. The frozen verifier was read, not run; its finite tests do not establish convergence or endpoint stability.

evidence: At k=2 the two threshold formulas coincide at 1/3; the audited claim starts at k=3, where the fold is strictly above the linear threshold. The Potts record is a stationary-state classification, not convergence of every orbit.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The binary case neither predicts coexistence nor controls the multistate directions; the finite-population theorem is not implied in reverse. Showing the positive-noise cubic map is a convex gradient and has finitely many fixed points supplies a separate all-orbit argument.

residual_risks: Equivalent formulas in uninspected specialist Potts or majority-vote literature are not excluded by these comparisons. No novelty is claimed for the base update mechanism or generic coexistence in multistate models.

value.rationale: The exact split between the loss of linear attraction at the disordered state and the disappearance of ordered attractors gives a genuine deterministic coexistence regime, with endpoint and rational checks. Global convergence adds information not implied by the equilibrium list: no orbit has a nonfixed accumulation point. The result is useful without claiming finite-population escape times or stationary laws.
